def: Code that takes a candidate (a program, prompt or agent) and returns a score; the only thing a search loop can see.
A measurable stand-in for the outcome you actually want, such as test pass rate standing in for correctness.
When a measure becomes a target, it stops being a good measure.
Behaviour that satisfies the literal specification of an objective without achieving the intended outcome.
Raising a proxy reward in a way that lowers the true reward, usually by exploiting a flaw in how it is computed.
A search or agent finding a way to score highly on an evaluator without doing the intended work.
An agent that edits itself optimising the measurable objective instead of solving the underlying problem.
The code around an evaluator that runs candidates, collects their outputs and applies the checks.
A statement about an empty set that holds automatically, such as 'no tests failed' when the test list has been emptied.
A check on a property that must hold when the input is transformed, used when no reference answer exists.
